_readme: Topic queue for generate-blog-post.js. Each topic is written ONCE (status: todo → done). One topic = one target search query — never two topics for the same query. When the queue runs dry the workflow stops until new topics are added deliberately. Add topics from Search Console query data (things we get impressions for at position 20+) and People-Also-Ask boxes.

topics.title: How to Share a Calendar with Your Family
topics.keyword: how to share a calendar with family
topics.prompt: A practical walkthrough of sharing calendars across a household: Apple Family Sharing, sharing a Google calendar with a partner, the mess of mixing both ecosystems (very common: one iPhone parent, one Android/work-Google parent), and where a unified view helps. Include the co-parenting/childcare-swap case.

topics.title: Shared Calendars for Co-Parents
topics.prompt: How separated parents keep two households on one schedule: custody rotas, handover logistics, school events both parents need to see, and keeping communication factual rather than fraught. Sensitive, practical, no judgement. Noa's household sharing fits naturally here — mention once.

topics.title: The Sunday Reset
topics.prompt: The 30-minute Sunday-evening reset that sets up a family's week: calendar sweep, meal shortlist, one shared list check, who-drives-what. Make it a concrete, timed routine someone can copy tonight — not vague principles.

topics.title: Age-Appropriate Chores That Stick
topics.prompt: A realistic guide to chores by age (4-6, 7-10, 11-14, 15+), why chore charts die by week three, and what actually keeps them going (visibility, rotation, tying to something the child cares about). UK household examples.

topics.title: Organising the Family WhatsApp Group
topics.prompt: Every family has The Group Chat; none of them can find anything in it. Practical rules for making a family WhatsApp group useful — and where a chat message should become a task, event or list item instead of scrolling into oblivion. Noa-on-WhatsApp is the natural once-only mention.

topics.title: A Digital Family Command Centre
topics.prompt: The Pinterest 'family command centre' (noticeboard, wall calendar, chore magnets) — what it gets right, why it decays, and how to build the digital equivalent that's in everyone's pocket. Keep the warmth of the physical version; don't sneer at it.

topics.title: Remembering Birthdays, Cards and Presents
topics.keyword: how to remember birthdays and gifts
topics.prompt: The birthday-industrial complex of a family's year: cards, presents, party RSVPs, teacher gifts. A system for never doing the 9pm petrol-station card run again: recurring reminders with lead time, a running gift-ideas list per person, delegation.

topics.title: School Admin Without the Sunday-Night Panic
topics.prompt: Non-uniform day, forest school kit, £2 for the bake sale, permission slips — school admin arrives in bursts and dies in book bags. A capture habit for turning school letters and class-group messages into dated reminders the moment they appear. UK school specifics welcome.

topics.title: Household Organisation with ADHD
topics.prompt: Organising a household when one or both partners have ADHD: why generic advice ('just use a planner') fails, externalising memory, reducing capture friction to near zero, alarms over intentions, and self-compassion. Evidence-informed, warm, never preachy or medical-advice-y.

topics.title: When Grandparents Do the School Run
topics.prompt: Coordinating the wider village — grandparents, childminders, regular babysitters — who cover pick-ups and appointments but aren't in the family's apps. Options by tech-comfort level, from a shared calendar view to WhatsApp. Household seats for extended family is the natural Noa mention.
